rationale: Required story AC on failure-toast content is unmet: createUser's catch always shows a fixed string instead of the backend's message (CR-006, critical). The role interdependency 'mirror UserDetailsPopup.tsx' requirement is only half-implemented: nothing disables Admin while Maintainer is on or Auditor while Admin/Maintainer is on, so an invalid role combination can be submitted (CR-004, CR-005, major). The form is never reset on close, so stale values resurface on reopen (CR-002, major), and there is no in-flight submit guard, unlike the sibling ResetBudgetPopup (CR-003, major). Test coverage is partial: no auditor-hidden or admin+local case (CR-001, major). All 6 candidates from the edge-case and acceptance lenses were verified against the live source and confirmed reachable; 0 deferred, 0 dismissed. Standards audit ran clean (commit-format pass, security pass, code-quality na — no guide/ArtifactRef); no coverage gap.

findings.title: Missing auditor-hidden and admin+local test cases
findings.problem: The test file covers hidden-for-non-privileged, hidden-for-admin-non-local, and visible-for-maintainer-local, but never asserts that an auditor (isAuditor: true) cannot see the button, nor that an admin (as opposed to a maintainer) sees it on a local-auth deployment.
findings.impact: Two of the acceptance criteria's explicitly-named role/mode combinations have no regression coverage; a future change could silently expose the button to auditors or hide it from admins without any test failing.
findings.recommendation: Add two cases to createUserButton.test.tsx: isAuditor:true + local auth renders no button, and isAdmin:true (non-maintainer) + local auth renders and opens it.

findings.title: Form values not reset on popup close/reopen
findings.problem: useForm() only destructures control/handleSubmit/setValue — no reset is called, no useEffect keys off isOpen, and UsersManagementPage.tsx mounts CreateUserPopup once with no remount key.
findings.impact: Closing the popup (cancel or after a successful create) and reopening it resurfaces the previous attempt's email/username/password and role-switch state, risking an admin unintentionally submitting stale role selections for a different user.
findings.recommendation: Destructure reset from useForm and call it in a useEffect keyed on isOpen (reset to defaultValues when isOpen becomes false), matching the reset-on-close pattern used elsewhere in this popup family.

findings.title: No guard against duplicate submit while in flight
findings.problem: onSubmit is async but nothing disables the Create button while the request is pending: formState.isSubmitting is not read and Popup's submitDisabled prop is not passed, unlike the sibling ResetBudgetPopup.tsx which tracks isSubmitting and passes submitDisabled={isSubmitting}.
findings.impact: A double-click or repeated Enter before the first POST /v1/admin/users resolves fires a duplicate create request.
findings.recommendation: Read isSubmitting from useForm's formState (or track local submitting state) and pass submitDisabled={isSubmitting} to Popup, mirroring ResetBudgetPopup.tsx.

findings.title: Auditor switch not disabled when Admin/Maintainer is on
findings.problem: The is_auditor Switch (lines 157-168) has no disabled prop. UserDetailsPopup.tsx disables its equivalent Auditor switch whenever roleFlags.is_admin || roleFlags.is_maintainer is true, but CreateUserPopup lets it be turned on regardless, and turning it on does not clear is_admin/is_maintainer.
findings.impact: A user can be created with is_auditor:true alongside is_admin:true or is_maintainer:true, an invalid role combination the edit flow (UserDetailsPopup) prevents by construction.
findings.recommendation: Disable the Auditor Switch when is_admin || is_maintainer is true, mirroring UserDetailsPopup.tsx's handleRoleChange/disabled logic.

findings.title: Admin switch not disabled when Maintainer is on
findings.problem: The is_admin Switch (lines 169-186) has no disabled prop. UserDetailsPopup.tsx disables its equivalent Admin switch whenever roleFlags.is_maintainer is true (an early-return in handleRoleChange enforces the same rule), but CreateUserPopup lets Admin be toggled off directly while Maintainer remains on.
findings.impact: A user can be created with is_maintainer:true and is_admin:false, an invalid role combination the edit flow forbids, and other code may assume the is_maintainer-implies-is_admin invariant holds.
findings.recommendation: Disable the Admin Switch when is_maintainer is true, mirroring UserDetailsPopup.tsx's handleRoleChange/disabled logic.

findings.title: createUser error toast ignores backend message
findings.problem: userStore.createUser's catch always calls toaster.error('Failed to create user') and never reads error?.parsedError?.message, so a specific backend validation reason (e.g. a password-policy violation) never reaches the admin/maintainer.
findings.impact: Fails the required story AC that a failure toast must surface the backend's message; the sibling UserProjectsTable.tsx:173 already establishes the correct pattern (toaster.error(error?.parsedError?.message || 'Failed to update role')) elsewhere in this same page area.
findings.recommendation: Change the catch to toaster.error(error?.parsedError?.message || 'Failed to create user'), matching UserProjectsTable.tsx's pattern.
